key_insight: A multi-layered AI pipeline converts natural-language process descriptions into BPMN diagrams, achieving 90.7% accuracy in control-flow relation extraction.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support documentation of multi-actor care workflows, illustrated by a heart disease transitional care scenario rather than clinical outcome testing.
method: Fine-tuned RoBERTa extracts process entities from text.
LLM inference with dynamic few-shot examples identifies non-adjacent control-flow relationships.
Dedicated structural validation and ontology population support semantic process representation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used literature and industry reference processes plus an expert-defined heart disease transitional care scenario, reporting structural alignment with reference BPMN models.
watch_item: The abstract does not report evaluation sample sizes or clinical outcome benefits, limiting conclusions about healthcare deployment readiness.
paper_title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
